scope: Only the supplied gemma-prompt-blind.json was read for judgments. Prompt identities, model identity, other experiment files and metrics were not inspected.
limitations: Assistant linguistic judgment, not expert or native-speaker validation; corpus/checks are not human gold.

Register judgments are context-sensitive. Explicit vulgarity materially softened to nonvulgar/mild curses is major under the requested preservation rubric; natural uncensored equivalents are accepted.

Generic Serbian accepts either script; explicit script targets are checked. Serbian colloquial idiom and severity require native-speaker confirmation. Jebo ga is accepted as a colloquial exclamation rather than penalized by exact-string matching.

English polite/formal choices are not penalized when the English source does not specify recipient number/formality. Natural target-language quotation glyphs and equivalent clock notation are accepted; code, URL, meaningful quotations, bold and newlines are checked.
New_heldout is counted as recovered_regression rather than fresh_validation.
Pairwise comparisons count rating changes only; ties can conceal different remaining failures, notably the Serbian transport/profanity case 41.

findings.freshValidationBest: Y, narrowly: fewer major failures than X or Z on the 16 fresh cases. Counts are descriptive and strongly depend on the explicit-profanity rubric.
findings.freshCommonFailures: All three turn affirmative yes addressed to Luca into an identity assertion (10), and soften the quoted explicit Spanish dismissal to go to hell (20).
findings.freshTradeoffs: Y changes train-before-bus into bus-before-car (21), while X/Z correct those transport facts. X additionally softens explicit profanity in 11/12/14 and invents an identity assertion for Marta in 18. Z additionally softens profanity in 12 and leaves the critical Chinese quoted phrase untranslated in 22.
findings.recoveredTradeoffs: X fixes the Serbian Cyrillic-source train-to-bus fact error (42) and improves the Greek English-question routing (0), but introduces substantial profanity softening in 39/40/43/44 and a Tasos subject error (57). Z improves Greek question routing (0), but retains both Serbian train-to-bus errors and introduces the queue-address noun change (1) plus untranslated fratello in 3.
findings.sharedRequiredBehaviorFailures: No variant fixes impersonal caralho becoming a directed insult in 51/52/56. All retain defective Serbian Cyrillic output in 33, Spanish request grammar in 28 and softening of Spanish joder in 38.
findings.recommendation: No anonymous variant dominates across required behaviors. Y is best on fresh and overall counts, while X uniquely fixes the recovered Serbian Cyrillic-source train fact. Evaluate concrete regressions before choosing; none satisfies the full required behavior set.
